# Atrial Fibrillation

This folder contains specific clinical quality indicators used by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to monitor the treatment and management of atrial fibrillation in Denmark. The metrics track long-term adherence to anticoagulation therapy at one, two, and five years post-diagnosis, the incidence of severe bleeding among prevalent patients, and the provision of structured patient education within the first year of diagnosis. Each page details the indicator's definition, national and regional performance against established standards, and the underlying registry data used for calculation.

## Pages

- [[indikator-4a1|Indikator 4a1]] — Measures the proportion of atrial fibrillation patients receiving indicated anticoagulation treatment one year after their index date.
- [[indikator-4a2|Indikator 4a2]] — Tracks sustained anticoagulation treatment coverage two years post-diagnosis to evaluate long-term guideline adherence.
- [[indikator-4a3|Indikator 4a3]] — Monitors five-year treatment persistence for anticoagulation, highlighting geographic variations and long-term cardiovascular care consistency.
- [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] — Surveils the incidence of severe bleeding among prevalent atrial fibrillation patients to evaluate the safety of anticoagulant therapy.
- [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] — Evaluates the proportion of newly diagnosed patients who receive a structured education program within their first year, tracking patient engagement and SKS coding compliance.
